description: Technical University of Munich and Stanford University researchers publish the PointER generation workflow for cropping building point clouds and linking energy features. The repository includes setup documentation, environment definitions, an example notebook and instructions for processing an area of interest. It uses national LiDAR, building footprints, district boundaries and UPRN coordinates. Python source is free under MIT. Its demonstrated coverage is 16 English districts, while new runs follow the user's source coverage and dates. Generated geometry can support building-stock and retrofit simulations with model-energyplus. A caveat is that the documented Verisk footprint input carries separate restrictions; the README identifies OpenStreetMap as an alternative. The workflow also requires substantial memory and upfront data preparation. Open code does not remove input-data obligations. No container was started or point cloud generated during this review.
